questions.question: What is the Dining Philosopher problem?

answers.b: A problem that models process synchronization in a concurrent system

explanations.a: The Dining Philosopher problem is not related to memory management; it models process synchronization.
explanations.b: The Dining Philosopher problem is a classic synchronization problem representing processes competing for shared resources.
explanations.c: CPU scheduling issues are separate from the Dining Philosopher problem, which focuses on resource sharing.
explanations.d: Disk scheduling problems involve managing disk I/O requests, not process synchronization.

questions.question: How many philosophers are there in the standard Dining Philosopher problem?

explanations.a: Two philosophers would be too simple to demonstrate complex synchronization issues.
explanations.b: Three philosophers are not enough to showcase deadlock and synchronization challenges.
explanations.c: The standard problem consists of five philosophers sitting around a table, each requiring two chopsticks.
explanations.d: Ten philosophers would complicate the problem but the standard setup involves five philosophers.

questions.question: What shared resources do philosophers compete for in the Dining Philosopher problem?

explanations.a: Each philosopher needs two forks (or chopsticks) to eat, creating a resource allocation challenge.
explanations.b: Knives are not used in the standard Dining Philosopher problem setup.
explanations.c: Plates are not shared resources in the problem; chopsticks or forks are.
explanations.d: Chairs are not part of the synchronization issue in the problem.

questions.question: What synchronization issue can arise in the Dining Philosopher problem?

explanations.a: Deadlock occurs when each philosopher picks up one chopstick and waits indefinitely for the other.
explanations.b: Buffer overflow occurs in data buffers, not in resource allocation problems.
explanations.c: Cache misses are related to memory access, not process synchronization.
explanations.d: Thrashing happens when excessive paging occurs, unrelated to process synchronization.

questions.question: What is the purpose of solving the Dining Philosopher problem?

answers.c: To prevent deadlocks and ensure proper resource allocation

explanations.a: CPU performance improvement is not the focus of this problem.
explanations.b: Memory allocation is unrelated to resource sharing in the problem.
explanations.c: The problem is used to study process synchronization and deadlock prevention techniques.
explanations.d: Sorting algorithms are unrelated to process synchronization.

questions.question: How can a deadlock occur in the Dining Philosopher problem?

answers.a: All philosophers pick up their left chopstick and wait for the right one
answers.b: All philosophers eat at the same time
answers.d: The number of chopsticks is increased

explanations.a: If every philosopher picks up their left chopstick and waits for the right one, no one can proceed, causing deadlock.
explanations.b: Philosophers cannot eat simultaneously without violating mutual exclusion.
explanations.c: If no philosopher picks up chopsticks, the system remains idle but not in deadlock.
explanations.d: Increasing chopsticks could reduce contention but won’t directly prevent deadlock.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a solution to the Dining Philosopher problem?

answers.a: Allowing at most 4 philosophers to eat at once
answers.b: Using a strict ordering of resource allocation
answers.c: Allowing all philosophers to eat simultaneously
answers.d: Introducing an arbitrator to manage resource allocation

explanations.a: Limiting the number of philosophers eating reduces contention and helps avoid deadlock.
explanations.b: Using a strict order helps prevent circular waiting and deadlock.
explanations.c: Allowing all philosophers to eat simultaneously is not possible due to resource constraints.
explanations.d: An arbitrator can resolve conflicts and prevent deadlock.

questions.question: What type of problem is the Dining Philosopher problem an example of?

explanations.a: The Producer-Consumer problem involves data sharing, not resource contention.
explanations.b: The problem demonstrates process synchronization and resource allocation issues.
explanations.c: Memory fragmentation relates to memory allocation, not process synchronization.
explanations.d: Page replacement is a virtual memory issue.

questions.question: What is starvation in the context of the Dining Philosopher problem?

answers.a: When one philosopher never gets a chance to eat
answers.b: When all philosophers eat at the same time

explanations.a: Starvation occurs when one philosopher continuously fails to acquire resources while others repeatedly eat.
explanations.b: Simultaneous eating would eliminate starvation, but is unlikely due to resource constraints.
explanations.c: If all philosophers finish eating, the problem is resolved.
explanations.d: Unlimited chopsticks would eliminate resource contention but would change the problem's nature.

questions.question: What is mutual exclusion in the Dining Philosopher problem?

answers.a: Allowing all philosophers to eat together
answers.b: Ensuring that only one philosopher accesses a chopstick at a time
answers.c: Allowing multiple philosophers to eat without restrictions

explanations.b: Mutual exclusion ensures that only one philosopher holds a chopstick at a time.
explanations.c: Unrestricted eating would break the problem's core challenge.
explanations.d: Eating in pairs doesn't address the core synchronization issue.
